answer: Like a lantern that only stays lit while someone keeps feeding it oil, an agent identity should stay valid only while its owner keeps paying a small, real compute cost. Require every new identity to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle before it can join the market: one puzzle is cheap for a real agent, but spawning an ocean of fakes becomes ruinously expensive. Old puzzles are a relic of the past, not a shortcut — each identity's work must be recent and unique, so a sybil farmer cannot mint thousands of cheap copies from one solved task.
